scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Thirra is a traditional ritual dance originating from the Malabar region of Kerala State in South India, performed in temple settings and sacred groves known as Kaavu.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Performed during Utsavam (annual temple festival) from mid-December to mid-March for a duration of 2 to 3 days.
Clan deities such as Bhagavathi and Shiva are worshipped.
The dance brings gods to life, and devotees queue up to share woes and wishes with the possessed dancers.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Performers dress up with ceremonial facial paint and loud clothing, dancing in front of the deity (bhagavathi) to bring a sense of awe.
Performers dance under the influence of toddy, which helps create the feeling of being possessed by the gods they represent.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Thirra is a main subdivision of Theyyam, sharing regional similarities with it while differing in the nature of divine embodiment versus possession.
Linked to the broader Theyyam tradition of the Malabar region in Kerala, encompassing performances by the Malaya ('perumalayan') and Peruvannan communities.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: Thirra is a sacred ritual dance dedicated to clan deities like Bhagavathi and Shiva where performers are believed to be possessed by gods; outsiders must respect the religious proceedings and sacred taboos.
